title: The Cinder Lark's Salvage Registry
summary: Your battered courier hull carries more patched bulkheads than original plates.
body: Registry records list The Cinder Lark as a light magi-tech courier decommissioned after the Ash-Line Skirmish. Three previous captains welded their own copper ley-busbars into her spine before she fell into your hands.
SABLE-7, the ship's surviving navigation intelligence, insists at least two of those captains never actually disembarked—their telemetry habits still echo in the nav-core.
unlockHint: Complete your cryo-pod intake aboard The Cinder Lark.

title: The Silt-Line & Inner Drift
summary: A rust-choked corridor of shattered freighters, gravel eddies, and desperate outposts.
body: Where the inner star-lanes thin out, iron dust and fractured moons gather in slow-turning eddies known as the Silt-Line. Navigation relies on amber beacon buoys and sheer nerve.
Outposts like Siltport survive by stripping derelicts before Syndicate customs cutters can slap a salvage lien on the wreckage.
unlockHint: Speak with Dockmaster Renn at Siltport Landing Pad.

title: The Ledger Syndicate's Tithe
summary: Corporate bailiffs who tax every liter of aether fuel and every weld on the rim.
body: Founded by Core-sector shipping magnates after the Collapse, the Ledger Syndicate enforces order through debt charters and orbital tariff cutters. Pay your tithe, and their beacons keep your lane clear.
Fall behind, and Collector Vane-Kael's inspectors impound your drive core—leaving your crew stranded in red dust.
unlockHint: Learn about the Syndicate's squeeze on Siltport.

title: Courier Brig Kestrel — Sealed Manifest
summary: The Kestrel wasn't hauling ore—she was carrying Pre-Collapse tuning schematics.
body: Official port logs claimed the Kestrel carried refined copper ingots. In truth, her aft ward-bubble held a Syndicate blackbox keyed to deep-rim harmonic beacons.
Whatever sheared her spine in the Inner Drift didn't use conventional plasma—the hull edges were vitrified into singing glass.
unlockHint: Breach and resolve the Kestrel Wreckage.

title: The Pre-Collapse Ley-Lattice
summary: Before the skies broke, starships rode woven rivers of resonant aether.
body: Centuries ago, the Architects braided star-lanes out of basalt obelisks and living rune-circuits, allowing vessels to glide between systems without burning raw shards.
When the Lattice shattered, most relays went silent—except in the Deep Frontier, where stray monoliths still answer ships carrying old-frequency keys.
unlockHint: Decode the Kestrel's blackbox.

title: Harmonic Aether Bleed
summary: Why dead relays sing—and why unshielded pilots hear voices in the static.
body: Raw aether shards store kinetic and psychic impressions alike. When a nav-core or ward-coil overheats near an anomaly, residual memories bleed across the ship's copper conduits.
Purists ground it out with cold iron; Aether-Bound pilots learn to read the melody.
unlockHint: Investigate the ghosts in The Cinder Lark's nav-core.

title: The Siltport Free Charter
summary: An outpost's fate hinges on who holds the gantry cranes and fuel ledgers.
body: Founded by three wreck-diving families, Siltport was promised independence under the Rim Accord—a promise the Ledger Syndicate quietly buried beneath emergency docking tariffs.
Whether Siltport stands free, kneels to the Syndicate, or runs a shadow-market truce depends on who controls the Kestrel leverage.
unlockHint: Confront Collector Vane-Kael during the Tariff Standoff.

title: The Singing Monolith
summary: Three hundred meters of matte-black basalt humming with forgotten coordinates.
body: Suspended upright in deep vacuum beyond the Syndicate buoys, the Singing Monolith predates every human and Vexari colony in the sector.
Its fluted faces wake only when answered by a resonant harmonic—revealing either a doorway to the wider stars or a wound best left sealed.
unlockHint: Reach and confront the Singing Monolith in the Deep Frontier.

title: Ash-Glass & Cantina Brokers
summary: Forbidden phase-weaves and stolen Syndicate ciphers traded over rust-gin.
body: Behind corrugated shutters in Rust & Cantina Row, hooded brokers press silver-etched wafers into oil drums. Half are counterfeit; the rest can bend plasma around a deflector shield.
Old Iron Bramwell says the best intel on the rim never touches a port terminal—it's whispered over a shared brazier.
unlockHint: Deal with the rumor brokers in Siltport's Cantina Row.

title: Echoes of the Void Choir
summary: Smugglers call them 'singing urns'—relays that remember the moment the Lattice fell.
body: Scattered across the outer reef are sealed ceramic-and-quartz urns recovered from Pre-Collapse listening posts. Even muffled in lead foil, they hum in three-part harmony.
The Syndicate pays handsomely to lock them away; the Choir's remnants pay even more to hear them sing.
unlockHint: Inspect contraband along Siltport's smuggling lanes.

title: The Rim Accord & Siltport's Debt
summary: A forgotten independence charter undermined by an emergency water-bailout rider.
body: Three wreck-diving families founded Siltport under the Rim Accord—a Core-sanctioned promise of free-port autonomy in exchange for keeping Inner Drift salvage lanes clear.

Seven years ago, when Siltport's main moisture vaporators failed during a dry-season dust siege, Dockmaster Renn signed an emergency Syndicate bailout rider. Collector Vane-Kael has used its compounding penalty clauses to strangle the port ever since.
unlockHint: Speak with Dockmaster Renn about Siltport's history.

title: The Tariff Wars
summary: Two decades ago, customs disputes turned into plasma broadsides across the Inner Drift.
body: Before the Ledger Syndicate perfected debt-charter enforcement, outer-rim guilds fought open skirmishes against corporate blockade cutters. Decommissioned Ironforged chassis and half the wrecks in the Silt-Line date back to those five bloody years.
When the guilds ran out of refined fuel, the Syndicate bought up the surviving drydocks—and made sure no independent captain could ever afford a fleet again.
unlockHint: Listen to Old Iron Bramwell's stories by the brazier.

title: Three Captains of The Cinder Lark
summary: Orlov, Tessa, and a nameless courier left more than weld-scars in your ship's spine.
body: Before The Cinder Lark drifted into your hands, three captains flew her: Captain Orlov, who braided her copper ley-conduits by hand; Captain Tessa, who vanished chasing a three-note harmonic past the Glass Shoals; and a silent courier who never logged a destination.
SABLE-7's diagnostic matrix was patched from all three pilots' flight recorders—which may explain why she occasionally hums a tune she never learned.
unlockHint: Ask SABLE-7 about The Cinder Lark's previous captains.

title: The Missing Fore-Hull
summary: Half of the courier brig Kestrel wasn't destroyed—it was carried deeper into the Drift.
body: Blackbox telemetry confirms the Kestrel suffered a violent harmonic shear, vitrifying her mid-deck into singing glass. Yet her forward bridge and cargo prow never broke up in the gravel eddy.
A single faint distress pulse—too weak for standard port dishes—pinged from the Mid-Drift hours after the shear, before going dark.
unlockHint: Decode the Kestrel's sigil-drive blackbox.

title: The Slag Foundry & Ironkin Clans
summary: An independent Ironkin smelter-barge turning Tariff War scrap into honest iron.
body: After the Tariff Wars left dozens of escort hulls drifting in the Mid-Drift, Ironkin engineers lashed two decommissioned ore-barges together and lit induction crucibles in open vacuum.
Forgemaster Durn's clan distrusts Syndicate bailiffs and Choir mystics alike—they trade only with captains who respect torque, fair weight, and kept promises.
unlockHint: Visit The Slag Foundry in the Mid-Drift.

title: Buoy 14 & The Anchor-9 Charter
summary: Why the Ledger Syndicate squeezes every rim port dry: a silent black-site in the deep reef.
body: Officially, Buoy 14 is a routine customs repeater logging docking tariffs. Inside its encrypted partition lies a different ledger: millions in rim tithes funneled into Deep Frontier quarantine station Anchor-9.
Collector Vane-Kael believes the Pre-Collapse Lattice caused the Collapse—and uses rim taxes to bankroll containment spikes before the Choir can wake it again.
unlockHint: Crack or raid Syndicate Buoy 14 in the Mid-Drift.

title: The Vitrifying Shear
summary: What happens when an experimental Choir relay-key fires inside an unshielded hull.
body: The Kestrel didn't fall to pirates or Syndicate gunnery. When her experimental relay-key resonated with the Singing Monolith, the resulting harmonic wave turned mid-deck steel into translucent glass in a fraction of a second.
Its forward half was flung cleanly into the Mid-Drift along the ley-current.
unlockHint: Resolve the Kestrel Fore-Hull anomaly.

title: The Glass Shoals
summary: A graveyard of vitrified ships surrounding the Deep Frontier's outer reef.
body: Whenever an uncalibrated vessel rides a broken ley-current too close to the Monolith, the harmonic backlash vitrifies steel into singing crystal.
Captain Tessa's Starling rests at the shoals' center—a warning and a breadcrumb trail for those who know how to listen.
unlockHint: Navigate The Glass Shoals in the Deep Frontier.

title: The Listening Abbey
summary: A hollowed comet where the Void Choir's last archivists tend the memory of the Lattice.
body: Far from the zealots Vane-Kael fears, the monks of the Listening Abbey are archivists who preserve Pre-Collapse star-charts and voice-urns.
They believe the Singing Monolith is a wounded keystone—and that shattering it with cold iron would doom the entire sector.
unlockHint: Visit The Listening Abbey in the Deep Frontier.

title: Black-Site Anchor-9
summary: The Ledger Syndicate's secret cold-iron weapons ring built to silence the Monolith.
body: Bankrolled by decades of rim tariffs, Anchor-9 mounts six orbital grounding lances designed to pierce the Singing Monolith's basalt core.
Vane-Kael built it out of genuine terror of a second Collapse—unaware that firing it could trigger the very shear he hopes to prevent.
unlockHint: Confront Anchor-9 in the Deep Frontier.

title: The Truth of the Collapse
summary: The Architects' Lattice didn't attack the stars—it was holding a deep-void rift closed.
body: Captain Tessa's telemetry reveals why the Singing Monolith keeps pulsing: it is one of the last intact anchor-nodes holding back a gravitational and aether shear in the Deep Frontier.
It can be harmonized back into balance, carefully anchored silent—or greedily bled dry at the sector's peril.
unlockHint: Recover Captain Tessa's Echo-Core from The Glass Shoals.
